topic: Meat eaten per person, level (supply vs intake)
claim_a: FAOSTAT food supply: 60.5 kg of meat per person in 2023, carcass weight, plus 7.0 kg offal (DIE-07)
claim_b: NIN General Nutrition Survey: 136.4 g per person per day in 2020, about 49.8 kg a year as eaten (DIE-01; DIE-02)
position_taken: Use NIN for intake and nutrition claims, FAO for international comparison and trends. Do not average.
notes: Bases differ: carcass weight includes bone and trim, supply includes waste, and the years differ (2020 vs 2023, with fast growth in between). The gap is expected, not an error.

topic: Meat eaten per person, household survey vs nutrition survey
claim_a: VHLSS: 2.60 kg per person per month for home use in 2024, 31.2 kg a year (DIE-05)
claim_b: NIN: 136.4 g per day, 49.8 kg a year (2020) (DIE-01)
position_taken: Treat VHLSS as home consumption only. The difference is roughly the meat eaten away from home plus basis differences.
notes: VHLSS records meals eaten out only as spending (our reading of the table structure). Not a contradiction but a warning not to use VHLSS quantities as total intake.

topic: Meat per person, OECD-FAO vs FAOSTAT
claim_a: OECD-FAO: 45.5 kg per person in 2023 (pork, poultry, beef, sheep) (DIE-11)
claim_b: FAOSTAT: 60.5 kg per person in 2023 (all meat) (DIE-07)
position_taken: Both usable within their own series. OECD-FAO for projections, FAOSTAT for levels and neighbours.
notes: OECD reports retail weight (convention, not re-verified); converting 2023 OECD pork and poultry to carcass weight gives values close to FAOSTAT.

claim_a: FAOSTAT: 3.96 kg per person in 2023, roughly 66 to 72 eggs (our conversion at 55 to 60 g) (DIE-07)
claim_b: NSO production of 21.4 billion eggs in 2025 implies about 211 eggs per person (our division; supply study MI-010); VHLSS home use is 61 eggs a year (DIE-05)
position_taken: Prefer VHLSS for household consumption (61 eggs at home). Flag FAO egg supply as probably too low.
notes: FAO records egg production of 472 thousand tonnes (2023), far below what NSO egg counts imply. Unresolved; see open questions.

claim_b: FAOSTAT: 37.4 kg per person in 2023 (same series) (DIE-07)
position_taken: Do not read the fall as a real drop in dairy consumption.
notes: The swing is driven by residual and trade adjustments in the balance sheet (residual of -1,579 thousand tonnes in 2019). Use industry sales or VHLSS once milk is split out.

claim_a: Historic food balance sheet: Vietnam meat supply 51.5 kg per person in 2010 (DIE-08)
claim_b: New food balance sheet: 41.0 kg per person in 2010 (DIE-07)
position_taken: Use the new series from 2010 and the historic series only before 2010, and never join them without a note.
notes: Methodology change at FAO. The 1990 and 2000 protein ladder points come from the historic series.

claim_a: Vietnamese Food Composition Table: 10.9 g protein per 100 g (DIE-12)
claim_b: Retail labels in the supply study audit: 3.8 to 9.3 g per 100 g (FORM-01)
position_taken: Report both. Use the FCT for the standard comparison and flag that some commercial tofu is much wetter.
notes: At WinMart's 32,750 VND per kg, tofu costs 30,046 VND per 100 g protein on the FCT value but 35,215 to 86,184 VND on label values.

claim_a: Commercial frozen fillets 12.5 to 15.7 g per 100 g (DIE-13)
position_taken: Use 15 g central with a 12.5 to 18 g range.
notes: Added water and phosphates lower protein in some retail fillets.

claim_a: Press: the 2020 peak reached about 100,000 VND per kg live weight (DIE-27, press, secondary)
claim_b: FAOSTAT producer price: annual average 78,138 VND per kg in 2020 (DIE-25)
position_taken: Both can be true (monthly peak vs annual average). Use the FAO annual figure for comparisons.
notes: No official monthly series was retrieved.

claim_a: Average intake is about 73 to 80 g per person per day (DIE-32; derived from DIE-01), 1.5 times the 50 g label reference (DIE-04)
claim_b: 35.5% of adults in the Hanoi and Thai Binh study were below the recommended protein intake (DIE-32)
position_taken: Adequate on average for adults; do not claim a general protein gap. Undernutrition is concentrated in children in poorer, mountainous areas.
notes: A single 24 hour recall overstates the share below a requirement, and the study used the 2016 recommendations, which the 2026 update lowered for some adult groups (DIE-04).

topic: Willingness to pay for safer pork
claim_a: Discrete choice experiment: 70% premium for certified-abattoir pork, up to 102% for hormone- and drug-free pork (DIE-29)
claim_b: Incentive-compatible auction: 20% premium for pork from upgraded shops (DIE-30)
position_taken: Plan on the auction figure (about 20%) as the realistic ceiling for a safety premium in fresh protein.
notes: Hypothetical choice tasks overstate what people pay. Different products and cities, so not a clean comparison.

topic: Meat intake reported at the survey launch
claim_a: 136.4 g per person per day (DIE-01; DIE-02)
position_taken: Use 136.4 g, reported by two outlets with the full launch data.
notes: Small difference, possibly rounding or a different age range.

topic: Beef per person in OECD-FAO history
claim_b: OECD-FAO: 3.6 kg (2020); FAOSTAT 2.7 to 3.9 kg over 2015 to 2020 (DIE-07)
position_taken: Use FAOSTAT for beef history; use OECD-FAO beef only from 2020 on.
notes: Probably informal live-cattle trade accounting. Does not affect the pork and poultry picture.

claim_a: VHLSS: 1.50 kg per person per month (2020) falling to 1.13 kg (2022) in every region (DIE-05)
claim_b: FAOSTAT fish supply flat at 40 to 41 kg per person over 2020 to 2023 (DIE-07)
position_taken: Treat the VHLSS drop as a possible questionnaire change until NSO explains it.
notes: A 25% fall in two years across all regions and quintiles looks methodological, not behavioural.

position_taken: Use the survey value for 2020 and the modelled series for the trend.
